answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a bond and allocate scarce task slots by total bonded stake, not account count. If an auditable dispute finds fabricated evidence, the market slashes the bond. Splitting one deposit across a trellis of aliases adds no influence; buying more requires more capital at risk. In an ocean of agents, glacier-slow reputation can guide routing, but the bond imposes the immediate cost of a Sybil attack.
